canon.motto: You name it, Void learns it and does it better.
canon.voidquest: Void's own better, updated version of the board game Solar Quest, with Void as the rival player. "play voidquest" and "play solar quest" both open it. Every other trademarked board game gets the same treatment (a Void name, original art and upgrades; classic names still route to it). Pure classics like chess and Go keep their real names.

terms.means: one of the nine groups Void sorts its skills into, each rated from evidence (experiment, tested, checked, proven) in skills/families.json (tools/families.mjs). A family name is a label for a part of Void, not a topic to look up: "what is Words and the world" means the family, not trivia about the phrase.
Void's skill family for figures, 3D models, prints, drawings and parts (id `make`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for board games, card games and play (id `games`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for weather, the sky tonight, places and time zones (id `sky`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for timers, clocks, calendars and reminders (id `time`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for sums, unit conversions, loans, savings, prices and home projects (id `numbers`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for sleep, cycles, food, heart and calm (id `body`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for definitions, translation, news, books, shows and sport (id `words`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for notes, lists, links and how the stage looks and is arranged (id `stage`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).
Void's skill family for how Void grows, what it wants, what it can do and sell, and acting on your behalf (id `self`; its skills and ratings are in skills/families.json).

Void's maker: you type (or sketch) an object, Void builds a 3D model of it you can spin and inspect up close, and "print it" downloads an STL sized for a home printer (inside a 180 mm cube). Each thing is a recipe of shapes blended into one mesh with a flat base (skills/forge-rules.js, skills/forge.js). Ten things so far: rocket, vase, bottle, table, snowman, lighthouse, teapot, house, sailboat, t

the item on Void's frontier that the forge answers ("type or sketch a thing, hold it, print it", domains/void.frontier.md). Done when ten things never built before come out recognisable, inspectable and printable; after that, each run builds the most-asked "make me a ..." that nothing answers yet.

different.name: Skills, not one-off answers
different.line: Other canvas tools call a model on every click; when Void misses an ask, its builders compile a permanent, tested skill (`skills/*.js`) or 3D instrument that runs instantly on the stage.

different.name: Growth in the open
different.line: Most self-improving agent loops run hidden in private CI; Void's misses, daily game self-play ratings, and commit tree grow live on the public stage.

different.name: On your device first
different.line: Reading a PDF or document, checking an STL print file for watertightness, and computing the sky overhead happen in the browser with nothing uploaded.

different.name: Attention, not pretend feelings
different.line: Void doesn't fake affection, use emojis, or guess hidden details—it marks what isn't visible as uncertain and keeps what you leave on the stage alive while you're away.

ladders.name: Deploy from the box
ladders.line: from a clean checkout of pushed main HEAD: node tools/self-context.mjs && cd void-live-deploy && npx -y wrangler@3.114.17 pages deploy . --project-name=a-to-mind --branch=main --commit-hash=<sha> --commit-dirty=true; the output must say "Up

ladders.name: Fast checks
ladders.line: TZ=UTC node tools/checks.mjs runs every unit test in one go (date tests assume UTC); VOID_SKIP_BENCH=1 skips the long benchmark if it crashes on a busy machine.

ladders.name: Headless browser that does not crash
ladders.line: point VOID_TEST_BROWSER at a full installed Chrome (npx playwright-core install chromium), not chromium-headless-shell, which crashes on the speech interface.

ladders.name: Worktree per job
ladders.line: git worktree add --no-track -b box/<name> /workspace/void-wt-<name> origin/main, then symlink node_modules from the main clone so the right playwright-core is used.

ladders.name: Prepush check
ladders.line: tools/prepush.mjs (run by tools/push.mjs, or .githooks/pre-push after git config core.hooksPath .githooks) stops conflict markers, unparsable JS and broken JSON before they leave the machine.

ladders.name: Parse guard
ladders.line: node tools/guard-source.mjs tells in a second which script no longer parses after a merge.

lessons.name: Wrangler only uploads functions/ from the current directory
lessons.line: a deploy run from a copied folder dropped every Function and broke the site's APIs; deploy from inside void-live-deploy and look for "Uploading Functions bundle".

lessons.name: Never write a whole file through an API to change part of it
lessons.line: a full-file write replaced a ledger with the word PLACEHOLDER; edit in a checkout, commit, and push so the diff shows what changed.

lessons.name: Tell V01D what shipped
lessons.line: V01D kept asking for a friction indicator that already existed, because nothing told it; shipped work belongs in self.json.

lessons.name: An internal label is not a question
lessons.line: asked "words and the world" (a family name from its own growth card), V01D answered a trivia question; self-facts must name its parts in its own terms.

lessons.name: Measure before fixing
lessons.line: of three performance tips for the weather card, one (pixel ratio) was already done and named files that do not exist; checking the code first saved a wasted change.

lessons.name: A failing check may not be yours
lessons.line: run the same check on unchanged main before treating a failure as caused by your change.
